barriers.description: Later-round testing required participants to have internet access at home to review the system, which constrained who could participate.
barriers.justification: Requiring home internet access limited participant recruitment and thus hindered designers' ability to facilitate user involvement and to understand the real-world context of use for the system.
barriers.reference_excerpt: As we moved to later rounds of user testing, it was also necessary for participants to have internet access at home to review the recording system before the usability session.

barriers.description: The participant sample was predominantly White and college educated, limiting designers' knowledge about diverse user needs.
barriers.justification: A non-diverse sample constrained the team's ability to manage user understanding and to specify user requirements for underrepresented groups, reducing confidence that design decisions met broader user needs.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Our sample was predominately White and college educated, reflecting the demographics of the region where our study took place. Further work is needed with individuals from more diverse ethnic and racial groups and from those with lower educational attainment levels.

barriers.description: Usability testing was conducted in controlled lab settings rather than in naturalistic environments.
barriers.justification: Testing in controlled settings prevented designers from fully understanding the real-world context of use and limited their ability to evaluate how the system would perform and be used in everyday settings.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Our project was conducted in controlled settings, where participants were asked to think aloud and received assistance, if needed, with tasks. Although this is important at this stage of user design, it does not reflect the user experience in naturalistic settings.

barriers.description: Task instructions were sometimes unclear (eg, participants opened external tabs), which inflated critical incidents and confounded usability measurement.
barriers.justification: Unclear task design and facilitation reduced the team's ability to reliably evaluate designs and to integrate valid feedback for iteration, hindering accurate assessment of usability.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Some participants may have been unclear on the task instructions related to finding additional information (opening tabs outside of the UI), which may have resulted in the higher reported critical incidents in round 5 relative to our other usability metrics, that is, high SUS scores and task completion rate.

barriers.description: Introduction of hyperlinks, filters, and advanced search caused user confusion—particularly among older adults unfamiliar with modern UI affordances—leading to critical incidents.
barriers.justification: Users' unfamiliarity with these UI elements hindered designers' ability to evaluate and iterate the features (integrate feedback & iteration and evaluate designs) because observed problems reflected user interpretation issues rather than clear design faults.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The greatest number of challenges was observed in round 4, where hyperlinks were added. This resulted in confusion in finding sections of audio recordings to play using tags and using associated hyperlinks to find further information. Although participants became comfortable with most features, some features such as hyperlinks, filters, and the advanced search caused some confusion in the final round of testing. These challenges may be explained by a lack of familiarity with the modern UI design...

barriers.description: All usability testing used a laptop-only interface, leaving mobile contexts untested.
barriers.justification: Limiting testing to laptops prevented designers from understanding mobile contexts of use and evaluating mobile-specific interactions, constraining the specification of user requirements and future iteration for mobile devices.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Finally, we used a laptop computer for all usability testing sessions, but we hope to create a mobile adaptive UI, which will require further testing.
